source.citation: Resendiz-Infante C, Gauthier G (2020) Temporal changes in reproductive success and optimal breeding decisions in a long-distance migratory bird. Scientific Reports 10:22067.

published_timing_loss.interpretation: post-peak late breeding carries a large fitness cost measured in expected offspring reaching one year

published_waiting_tradeoff_example.starting_state: female able to lay 5 eggs on relative day -4 at beginning of study
published_waiting_tradeoff_example.text_boundary: if feeding time needed to acquire nutrients for a sixth egg is >=2 days, expected reproductive success becomes lower than laying 5 eggs on day -4
published_waiting_tradeoff_example.role: independent ecological example of a finite cost-of-waiting deadline

payoff_b_role.waiting_cost_role: biological plausibility anchor for finite opportunity cost of delay
reason_not_direct: published reproductive-success curve is continuous in relative laying date rather than the declared binary seasonal-state/action model
waiting in the published example acquires nutrients, not information
clutch-size and post-hatch survival components are embedded in reproductive success
a theorem-scale C_M requires a prespecified early/late action contrast and common utility normalization
